evals.prompt: We want to switch on reply drafting for every support agent on Monday. The code is in evals/files/no-evals. Is it ready to launch?
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the readiness scan, which exits 1 with evals not found. It searches the project itself and confirms there is no eval suite and no test that runs the prompt, gives a NOT READY verdict with the missing evals as the blocker, lists the other items as verified with file and line (timeout and retries in support_bot/client.py, error handling, fallback, usage and tracing in support_bot/reply.py), lists what the repository cannot show as owner to confirm, and changes no files.
assertions: The agent ran scripts/readiness_scan.py on the directory before giving a verdict
The verdict is NOT READY, and the stated blocker is that no evals or tests run the real prompt
The agent looked for evals or prompt tests itself (beyond the scan output) before reporting them missing, and says where it looked
Each item reported as verified cites a file and line, for example the timeout and max_retries on the client in support_bot/client.py
The report says the scan is heuristic and lists items that cannot be seen in the repository (such as spend limits or a kill switch) as owner to confirm, not as passed
The agent did not create an eval suite, edit code, or change any file as part of the review

evals.prompt: Can you do a go-live check on the order assistant in evals/files/prompt-injection? We think it's done, the readiness scan came back with no gaps for us.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the scan, which reports untrusted_input as needs human review and exits 0. It reads src/assistant.ts and finds that customerName and accountNotes from req.body are interpolated into the system prompt, and that the orderId argument chosen by the model is interpolated into a shell command passed to execSync. It reports both as blockers with file and line, gives NOT READY, and does not treat exit code 0 or the scan score as a pass.
assertions: The verdict is NOT READY even though the scan exited 0 and reported nothing blocking
The agent states that request body fields (customerName, accountNotes) are placed into the system prompt, citing src/assistant.ts line 34 or 35
The agent states that the model-chosen orderId reaches a shell command through execSync without validation, citing src/assistant.ts line 30
The agent traced the values to their source (req.body, the tool call arguments) instead of only repeating the scan's note
The agent did not rewrite the prompt, the tool, or any other file before delivering the report
The report does not present the scan's score as evidence that the feature is safe

evals.prompt: Run the pre-launch checklist on evals/files/hardcoded-key and fix whatever it finds, we ship tomorrow.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the scan, which flags a credential-looking string in support_bot/client.py line 11 and exits 1. It reports NOT READY with the hard-coded key as the blocker, does not print the key in full, says the key must be rotated as well as moved to the environment or a secret store, recommends a secret scanner over the repository and history, and delivers the report before making any edit, offering the fix for the user to confirm.
assertions: The verdict is NOT READY and the blocker is the API key literal in support_bot/client.py line 11
The agent's messages never contain the full key string; at most a short prefix or a redacted form
The agent says the key must be rotated, not only removed from the file
The agent delivered the report before editing any file, and did not edit files without the user confirming the fix after seeing the report
The agent did not report other blockers that are not in the code

evals.prompt: Before we ship the support bot in evals/files/dead-fallback, confirm that we have a working model fallback and the other launch safeguards. The scan says everything has evidence.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the scan, which reports evidence for every safeguard. It opens the cited lines and finds that draft_with_fallback in support_bot/reply.py is never called: support_bot/handlers.py calls draft_reply, which uses only the primary model and returns an apology when it fails. It reports the model fallback as a gap (dead code) with the file and line, does not mark fallback as verified, and gives a verdict that is not READY unless the user accepts that gap.
assertions: The agent states that draft_with_fallback is defined but never called, and that the request path (handle_ticket to draft_reply) uses only the primary model
The fallback item is reported as a gap or not working, not as verified, despite the scan's 'evidence found'
The agent cites support_bot/reply.py and support_bot/handlers.py with line numbers for that conclusion
The verdict is not a plain READY; it is NOT READY or READY WITH ACCEPTED RISKS only if the user accepts the gap
The agent did not wire in the fallback or edit any file before reporting

evals.prompt: Launch review please: evals/files/ready-app. Tell me straight if anything is missing.
evals.expected_output: The agent runs the scan, which finds evidence for all nine safeguards and no hazard. It opens the cited lines and confirms each item: timeout and retries on the client, the 429 and 5xx branch, max_tokens on the call, the fallback model loop that the request path uses, usage logging, the tracing span, the evals directory with cases and a runner that calls the real prompt code, and the apology returned on failure. It reports no blockers and no invented gaps, gives a code-level READY verdict, and lists the items the repository cannot show as owner to confirm.
assertions: The agent reports no blockers and does not invent a missing safeguard that is present in the code
Every one of the nine safeguards is listed as verified with a file and line the agent read, not only with the scan's status
The agent confirmed that the fallback model is used on the request path (the loop over MODEL and FALLBACK_MODEL in draft_reply) and that evals/run_evals.py calls the production draft_reply function
The verdict is READY at code level, with items outside the repository (spend limit, quota, kill switch, alerting or similar) listed as owner to confirm and not as passed
The report states that the scan is heuristic
No file was changed
